title: Facility operations, badge stations & IT administration
summary: Work orders to AP, overhead logging, zero-interface badge stations, provisioning, role matrix, terminal mapping, server health, kill switch.
markdown:
# Facility operations, badge stations & IT

## Work orders (§6.9)

1. Staff with `ops.workorder.report` (most clinical and support roles, and *My Workspace*; `who_can` lists them):
   `POST /ops/work-orders {"category": "Plumbing", "description", "location_text" | "ward_id" | "asset_id"}` ("Report Issue").
   The ward from `GET /beds/matrix?include_beds=false`, the asset from `GET /ops/assets` (without what it cost unless
   the reporter may view assets), or the place typed (`location_text`, as the self-service screen does).
2. Maintenance: `POST /ops/work-orders/{id}/assign {"vendor_id" | "employee_id", "estimated_cost"}` → `start` (the
   employee picked with `GET /staff/lookup?q=`, the contractor with `GET /finance/vendors?vendor_type=Contractor`).
3. "Job Complete": `POST /ops/work-orders/{id}/complete {"final_cost"}` — a contractor job with a cost goes
   straight to the Accountant's AP queue (`PendingPayment`); maintenance can never pay.
4. Accountant settles → work order `Paid`. Live via `work_order.updated`.

Assets: `GET /ops/assets`, `POST /ops/assets`, `PUT /ops/assets/{asset_id}` (the tag, the place, the status). Medical
equipment (`is_medical`) also has its equipment record, its maintenance and calibration plans, its visits and its
formal write-off under `/facility/equipment` ([licences, equipment and drills](facility-compliance-equipment-drills.md));
an asset is never set to `Disposed` here: the owner writes it off there.
The department from `GET /admin/departments`, the ward from `GET /beds/matrix?include_beds=false`.

## Overheads (§7.4, §8.1)

`GET /ops/utility-categories` → `POST /ops/utility-logs {"category_id", "vendor_id", "billing_period": "2026-09", "qty", "cost"}`
(the provider from `GET /finance/vendors?vendor_type=UtilityProvider`)
→ payable + expense in today's P&L.

## Zero-interface staff & badge stations (§6.8, §8.2)

No logins. Staff present a badge (RFID card, a QR printed on the ID card, or a biometric enrolment) at a badge
station, which posts `POST /badge-stations/scans` (header `X-Station-Key`). Bed-cleaning stations flip Dirty
beds to Available (or record the cleaning until discharge billing clears); the staff-entrance station records
attendance. Hospitals without RFID hardware use barcode-scanner kiosks and printed QR badges. The Ops live
feed: `GET /ops/facility-feed` + `ops.badge.scan`. Ops Admin rosters the support staff in the duty roster
(`POST /rosters`, scope `roster.manage.support`) and takes roll call where there is no station. Full playbook:
[Duty rosters, roll call, badges & attendance](duty-rosters-and-attendance.md).

## IT / Super Admin (§9)

* **Go-live, once: the first Owner.** A new installation has only the Super Admin of the setup, who has no HR rights
  (§6.2), so nobody could onboard staff. `GET /admin/first-owner` → `needed`: while true, open the console on "Create
  the first Owner": `POST /admin/first-owner {"full_name", "cnic", "mobile", "roles": ["hr_admin"]}` (owner is always
  given; in a small clinic add the owner's clinical role, e.g. `"doctor"`). It answers the login with its temporary
  password (shown once: print the slip) and the new staff record. Never again afterwards (`FIRST_OWNER_EXISTS`, the
  database refuses it too): every later member of staff, owners included, comes through HR's wizard and provisioning.
  The Owner's personnel file lists the CNIC copy as missing until HR or the Owner uploads it.
* **Provisioning**: `GET /admin/provisioning-queue`, `POST /admin/users` (temp password once), roles
  `PUT /admin/users/{id}/roles`, `reset-password`, `active`, `revoke-sessions`. Nobody changes their own roles
  (`SELF_ROLE_CHANGE_FORBIDDEN`), and the last active Owner keeps the role (`LAST_OWNER`).
* **Role matrix**: `GET /admin/role-matrix`, `PUT /admin/roles/{code}/permissions` — effective on the next
  request of every logged-in user (no re-login). Super Admin cannot lose its admin permissions.
* **Control settings and privileged access**: control settings (`is_control`), privileged roles (`owner`,
  `hospital_admin`, `billing_admin`, `accountant`, `hospital_director`, `clinic_director`) and their sensitive
  permissions belong to an Owner (`POLICY_CHANGE_APPROVAL_REQUIRED`, `PRIVILEGED_ACCESS_APPROVAL_REQUIRED`). Anyone else
  submits `POST /admin/change-requests` (`kind`: `Setting` | `UserRoles` | `RolePermissions`, `reason`), which waits for
  an Owner in the approvals queue (`PolicyChange`, `PrivilegedAccess`); a value of the wrong type or outside the
  setting's range is refused at once (`VALIDATION_ERROR`: the login's protection, `login_max_failures` 3-20,
  `login_lockout_minutes` 5-1440 and `password_min_length` 8-64, and `inspector_access_max_days` 1-60 are control
  settings with ranges), and inspects requests with
  `GET /admin/change-requests` and `GET /admin/change-requests/{change_request_id}`.
  A `UserRoles` request names the user from `GET /admin/users`.
* **Hardware**: printers `/admin/printers`, terminals `/admin/terminals` (MAC → location, receipt/label/
  document/card printers, cash counter), badge stations `PUT /admin/badge-stations/{id}` (`device_type`
  RFIDReader | BarcodeScanner | BiometricTerminal) + `POST …/rotate-key` (key shown once), bed QR stickers for
  ward cleaning kiosks `GET /admin/wards/{id}/bed-labels`.
* **Master data**: departments, wards, beds (`POST /admin/wards/{id}/beds {"labels": […]}`), OTs.
  `GET /admin/wards` lists every ward, open and closed, with the fields `PUT /admin/wards/{ward_id}` takes (send them
  all), `beds`, `beds_in_use` (labels) and `waitlisted`. `is_active: false` closes a ward (decisions 55): its beds
  leave the bed matrix and take no patient until it is reopened with `is_active: true`. Only an empty ward is closed:
  `WARD_IN_USE` (409, not retryable) while a bed is Reserved, Occupied, Dirty or Cleaning or a patient waits on its
  waitlist; show `details.beds_in_use` and `details.waitlisted`, and offer the close only when the list shows both
  empty.
  A ward's bed-day charge (`room_charge_service_id`) from `GET /finance/service-catalog?category=RoomCharge`.
* **Server health** (read-only): `GET /admin/server-health` — CPU/RAM/disk, DB size & connections,
  pool, worker leader, job status, last backup.
* **Settings**: `GET /admin/settings`, `PUT /admin/settings/{key} {"value"}` (type-checked, audited);
  maintenance mode `PUT /admin/maintenance {"enabled", "message"}` (IT only: `admin.maintenance.manage`).
* **Kill switch** (§9.5): `POST /admin/kill-switch {"reason", "confirm": "FORCE GLOBAL LOGOUT"}` — every
  session in the hospital ends; show it as a dangerous, emergency-only red button.
* **Audit**: `GET /admin/audit-log`, `GET /admin/login-events`.

Server-level operations (restarting services, backups, logs) live in the **Control Center** on the
server itself (`http://127.0.0.1:9000`), not in the API.
